issue.title: Persist the diff-badge signature and classification result on the agent-artifact index row
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 4 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

Epic sase-k3 phase sase-k3.3 took persisted diff-badge classification (diff_has_real_edits and linked_file_change_hint) off ACE's agents loader and moved it into a coalesced background pass scoped to visible rows, with carry-over across reloads. That removed ~0.40 s from first paint but did not remove the work — it relocated it, and it is still redone once per process.

Measured on athena at master 1f388edee across 9 real-terminal sessions (~/.sase/perf/tui_trace.jsonl, span agents.diff_badge_classification, source=apply):

  candidates: 11-12 visible rows per session
  duration: min 417 ms, p50 643 ms, max 1035 ms

That is the new user-visible badge-settle latency the deferral introduced, paid once per ACE session. Persisted diffs are immutable, so this is parsed once per process today when it could be parsed once per machine.

Scope: store the diff-badge signature (the identity the classification is valid for) and its result on the artifact row in the Rust core, so ACE reads a stored badge instead of re-reading diff bytes. The proposing plan is explicit that this belongs in the core rather than as a third frontend-side cache — sase already has DiffBadgeResultCache (in-process, sase-k3.3) and diff_has_real_edits' (path, mtime_ns, size) cache in src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_diff_badge.py.

Input to the schema design, per the plan: phase sase-k3.3 was asked to confirm or refute the research's suspicion that the byte volume concentrates in the linked-commit branch (_classify_linked_commit_diffs -> agent_commit_diffs). Its close note reports the linked-commit branch is NOT where the volume concentrates, but qualifies that dedup through the shared DiffBadgeResultCache collapses it before scheduling either way. Treat that as a partial answer: re-measure the per-branch byte volume directly before choosing what to key the stored signature on, rather than inheriting either the research's claim or sase-k3.3's qualification.

Work in sase-core through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first. Do not hand-edit the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml.
